results.title: Reporting obligations after a cybersecurity incident
results.text: 4. A covered entity that experiences a cybersecurity incident relating to its information system that has resulted in a material loss of control, compromise, unauthorized disclosure of data or information, or any other similar occurrence shall:

results.title: Definition: Cybersecurity incident
results.text: (d) “Cybersecurity incident” means any act in which a person has gained unauthorized access to an information system of a covered entity for the purpose of disrupting, disabling, destroying, or controlling the system or destroying or gaining access to the information contained therein.

results.title: Policy
results.text: 1. In accordance with the public policy of the State set forth in NRS 463.0129 and the requirements set forth in chapter 603A of NRS, it is critical that gaming operators take all appropriate steps to secure and protect their information systems from the ongoing threat of cybersecurity incidents. Gaming operators must not only secure and protect their own records and operations, but also the personal information of their patrons and employees as defined in NRS 603A.040.

results.title: Definition: Covered entity
results.text: (f) “Covered entity” means an entity required to comply with the requirements of this section. Each of the following qualifies as a covered entity: (1) Holder of a nonrestricted license as defined in NRS 463.0177 who deals, operates, carries on, conducts, maintains, or exposes for play any game defined in NRS 463.0152; (2) Holder of a gaming license that allows for the operation of a race book; (3) Holder of a gaming license that allows for the operation of a sports pool; and (4) Holder of a gaming license that permits the operation of interactive gaming.

results.title: Definition: Risk assessment
results.text: (h) “Risk assessment” means the process of identifying, estimating, and prioritizing risks to organizational operations and assets resulting from the operation of an information system. Guidance for conducting a risk assessment can be found in the Framework for Improving Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity, version 1.1 or later, published by NIST.

arguments.rationale: Sign-in from unusual IP 203.0.113.45 by j.alvarez on HTL-PMS-02 at 03:15 UTC [SIG-0006], followed by PowerShell query of PMS config [PRC-0002], sqlcmd queries to LOY-DB-01 [PRC-0003], data export to CSV [PRC-0004], and curl upload to external IP [PRC-0005] demonstrate unauthorized access beyond the user's normal duties.

The attacker exfiltrated 1.78 GB to external IP [NET-0003], exported player data to CSV [PRC-0004], and uploaded zip to external IP [PRC-0005]. The unusual sign-in [SIG-0006] indicates loss of normal control. This constitutes material loss of control or compromise.

Data exfiltrated to external IP 198.51.100.77: 1.78 GB network flow [NET-0003], player data exported to CSV [PRC-0004], and player data zip uploaded via curl [PRC-0005]. These constitute unauthorized disclosure of data.

No evidence found that gaming operations were disrupted. The accessed host HTL-PMS-02 is not gaming-critical [lookup_asset], and the slot management systems SLOT-DB-01 and SLOT-MGMT-01 show no related activity. Player loyalty database LOY-DB-01 is marked "Not part of game play."

The exported player data CSV [PRC-0004] and uploaded zip [PRC-0005] contain player club accounts and play history from LOY-DB-01, which the asset lookup confirms includes player personal information. The external transfer [NET-0003] discloses this data.

The last attacker activity was at 03:36 UTC [PRC-0005], the alert was raised at 16:58 UTC the same day, and the host has not shown further activity since. No evidence of persistence or reconnection after the exfiltration.

arguments.summary: At approximately 02:31 UTC on 2026-03-14, an unauthorized party accessed the hotel property management server HTL-PMS-02 via a sign-in from IP 203.0.113.45 by user j.alvarez [SIG-0006]. Between 02:31 and 03:36 UTC, the actor executed PowerShell to query PMS configuration [PRC-0002], used sqlcmd to query and export player club data from the loyalty database LOY-DB-01 to a CSV file [PRC-0003, PRC-0004], and subsequently uploaded a compressed archive of that data to external IP 198.51.100.77 via curl [PRC-0005, NET-0003]. This activity resulted in unauthorized access, compromise, and disclosure of personal information [SIG-0006, PRC-0004, PRC-0005, NET-0003]. No evidence indicates gaming operations were disrupted or that the attacker remains present.
